Part 1: Departmental Rationale & Tripartite Architecture

The History Department prioritises meaningful, manageable, and motivating feedback, focusing on high-impact live intervention, whole-class modelling, and structured pupil self-regulation over performative red-pen marking. Our feedback system is integrated into a unified Tripartite Curriculum Model:

Pillar 1: Master Textbooks

Pure narrative reading anthologies (zero source boxes, zero rubrics) providing immersive, high-challenge prose during whole-class reading before writing begins.

Pillar 2: Pupil Workbooks

16–20 page saddle-stitch workbooks. Verso: 5-Stage Chronological Inquiry Spine; Recto: Disciplinary writing on calibrated ~7.8mm–8.1mm ruled handwriting lines.

Pillar 3: Retrieval Companions

8-page (KS3) and 16–28 page (GCSE) companions featuring Domino causal flowcharts, 2-line dual retrieval, and self-scoring Marking Banks.

Centring Pupil Voice & Live Metacognition

Feedback is an active dialogue, not a retrospective teacher chore. Live marking during circulating coaching prompts pupils to vocalise historical reasoning, correct misconceptions in real time with green pen, and complete end-of-unit reflection grids in their workbooks to document progress and set immediate targets.

Zero Knowledge Giveaways in Scaffolds

Sentence stems and connectives in pupil workbooks provide purely structural, disciplinary scaffolding—never factual answers. Key Terms banks supply technical vocabulary (e.g. Diktat, Article 231, £6.6bn reparations), but connectives remain strictly content-free (e.g. In particular, a decisive factor was...), forcing pupils to retrieve historical knowledge from memory rather than transcribing hints.

Frequency of Marking

Key Stage 3

Routine classwork is reviewed via live circulating coaching and self-marking with the Knowledge Retrieval Companion's Marking Bank. Teachers assess one substantial disciplinary extended writing task (Explain Why 12m, Narrative Account 8m, or Interpretations 8m) per half term using the 5 Pathway Levels.

Key Stage 4 (GCSE)

Regular low-stakes rehearsals using Pearson Edexcel past questions. Teachers provide live exemplar modelling and mark formal timed assessments across Paper 1 (Medicine & Western Front), Paper 2 (Elizabeth & Middle East), and Paper 3 (Weimar & USA) against Pearson 9–1 mark criteria and CAT4 benchmarks.

Part 2: Standards, Grading & Feedback Types

Types of Marking & Feedback

1. Live In-The-Moment Coaching

Teacher circulates while pupils write on ruled lines, checking historical precision and intervening immediately with verbal coaching and green-pen margin codes.

2. Retrieval Companion Self-Scoring

Pupils complete low-stakes starters and self-mark immediately using the verified Marking Bank at the back of the companion, cementing factual recall and schema retention.

3. Disciplinary Writing Assessment

End-of-enquiry written pieces are assessed against national progression criteria (KS3) or Pearson Edexcel 9–1 criteria (GCSE), recorded on the workbook back cover ledger.

4. Spaced App Quizzing & QR Retrieval

Dual-QR codes on workbook back covers link pupils directly to interactive 20-question digital quizzes on the History Revision Hub, automating diagnostics and homework retrieval.

Spelling, Punctuation & Grammar (SPaG)

Consistent whole-school marking symbols applied across all humanities written work:

Symbol Meaning Symbol Meaning
Sp Incorrect spelling (write 3x in margin) ^ Word omitted
P Punctuation error (. , ! ?) ? Meaning unclear / historical confusion
G Grammar error / sentence structure ! Factual / chronological inaccuracy
C Capital letter required (proper noun/date) ✓ Valid historical evidence / explanation
// New paragraph required ✓✓ Exceptional analytical insight / causal link

Assessment & Grading Framework

Progress tracking is maintained using the ledger on the inside front/back cover of workbooks, aligned to national standards and indicative GCSE outcomes:

Pathway Level Score Band Indicative GCSE Disciplinary Writing Standard
GD (Greater Depth) 80% – 100% Grades 8 – 9 Sustained causal argument, conceptual hierarchy, nuanced evaluation.
Exp + (Expected +) 60% – 79% Grades 6 – 7 Consistent analytical structure, detailed evidence deployment, clear links.
Exp (Expected) 40% – 59% Grades 4 – 5 Accurate historical knowledge, structured explanation, sound PEEL points.
EM + (Emerging +) 30% – 39% Grade 3 Descriptive accounts, basic causal awareness, emerging terminology.
EM (Emerging) 10% – 29% Grades 1 – 2 Fragmentary recall, simple narrative statements requiring teacher guidance.

Part 3: Exemplar Implementation & Visual Evidence (Key Stage 3)

Visual Appendix • KS3

Key Stage 3 workbooks embed our double-page spread architecture: Verso inquiry spine [1.1]–[5.5] with left-trigger keywords; Recto writing tasks on calibrated ~7.8mm–8.1mm handwriting pitch with zero knowledge giveaways in scaffolds.

Figure 1: Progress & Assessment Ledger (KS3 Workbook). Lesson-by-lesson audit trail recording Effort (1–5), Pathway Standard (EM to GD), and formative teacher/pupil dialogue.
Dual-Pathway Centrefold Timeline

The centrefold (Pages 8–9 or 10–11) features our Panoramic Living Timeline with a binary dual-coding protocol:

  • Choice A (Visual Dual-Coding): Pupils draw a symbolic icon representing the decisive causal mechanism.
  • Choice B (Concept Mind Map): Pupils construct a 3-branch analytical web linking cause, event, and consequence.
Effort Scoring Rubric (1–5)
Score Pupil Focus & Diligence
5 • Exemplary Proactive curiosity; voluntary extension; exceptional pride.
4 • Good Consistent engagement; thoughtful contributions; complete work.
3 • Satisfactory Meets baseline; requires occasional prompting.
2 • Inconsistent Incomplete written tasks; frequent off-task reminders.
1 • Concern Persistent passivity; triggers departmental intervention.

Part 4: Exemplar Implementation & Visual Evidence (Key Stage 4)

Visual Appendix • KS4

At Key Stage 4, feedback is structured around Pearson Edexcel exam question tariffs, PEEL writing frames with content-free connectives, and targeted question intelligence:

Figure 3: Key Topic Assessment & Progress Record (Edexcel Medicine & Western Front Workbook, Page 28). Lesson-by-lesson audit tracking Pearson Edexcel exam question tariffs (Q1 4m Features, Q2a 8m Utility, Q2b 4m Follow-Up), pupil scores, and targeted teacher next steps.
Specification-Specific Question Tariffs
  • Paper 1 (Western Front): Feature questions exist strictly as two separate 2-mark questions: Q1(a) [2m] and Q1(b) [2m].
  • Paper 2 (Elizabethan): Two distinct 2-mark feature questions: Q1(a) [2m] and Q1(b) [2m].
  • Paper 2 (Middle East): Updated single 4-mark consequence format ('Explain one consequence of...').
Provenance Clues ('How Useful' Utility Prompts)

Scaffolding boxes guide students to evaluate Author (access, expertise), Audience (private diary vs mass propaganda), and Motive (substantive purpose) against verified historical context, eliminating generic speculation.
